prompt: This is the product-search endpoint of an e-commerce backend. The `products` table has grown to several million rows, and this search — a substring match typed into a search box — has become the slowest endpoint in the system, with latency climbing roughly linearly as the table grows. A developer already tried to fix it by adding an ordinary B-tree index on the searched column, but the query plan still shows a full table scan and nothing got faster. Explain why that index doesn't help here, and propose how you'd actually optimize this access pattern.
givenCode:
-- `products` has grown to several million rows; this search endpoint has become the slowest in the system
CREATE TABLE products (
    id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    price       NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
-- ~4,200,000 rows currently loaded

-- A developer already tried to fix the slow search by adding an ordinary
-- B-tree index on the searched column:
CREATE INDEX idx_products_name ON products (name);

-- The search box runs this query on every lookup, substring-matching a
-- user-typed fragment against the product name:
SELECT id, name, price
FROM products
WHERE name LIKE '%' || $1 || '%';
-- e.g. with $1 = 'phone':
-- SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%phone%';

-- EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%phone%';
--
--  Seq Scan on products  (cost=0.00..142853.00 rows=421 width=48) (actual time=0.031..1822.447 rows=396 loops=1)
--    Filter: (name ~~ '%phone%'::text)
--    Rows Removed by Filter: 4199604
--  Planning Time: 0.112 ms
--  Execution Time: 1822.501 ms
--
-- idx_products_name never shows up in the plan — it's still a full
-- sequential scan, and the same holds on other relational engines too.
